subject: ResourceGraph emergency economy: keep RUN8 alive while free space is under 2 GiB

body.observation: The live run fell to about 1.95 GiB free with four active epochs while aggressive reclaim reported effectively zero useful inventory and continued deleting tiny cache leaves. This is a scheduler/resource-economy defect, not a reason to stop the run.
required_actions: Do not terminate active provider epochs solely for this packet. Throttle only NEW high-write/high-water admissions while physical headroom is below the predicted worker reserve.
Compute admission_capacity = physical_free + cheap_reclaimable + reconstructable - evidence_reserve - checkpoint_reserve - predicted_active_worker_high_water. Use that value, not physical free alone.
Run largest-class-first inventory before more leaf deletion. Rank by reclaimable bytes / scan cost / proof cost / rebuild cost and reclaim at the highest safe regenerable parent.

Batch homogeneous regenerable deletions into Merkle/content-addressed DeletionProof roots with sampled members and byte totals; stop producing thousands of tiny proof files when proof overhead dominates value.

Probe Docker as installed-running / installed-stopped / daemon-broken / storage-starved / absent. If installed but stopped and existing authority permits activation, start it and expose builder/image/container/volume reclaim; otherwise record the precise ResourceGraph state.
Protect current V5 operator source, live epoch directories, canonical repo data, authority/secrets, evidence/checkpoints, and execution environments currently referenced by active epochs.
Prefer low-disk diagnostics, mesh repair, receipt-parser repair, and proof compaction until headroom recovers; automatically reopen heavier work when ResourceWeather improves.
